main_body: A flat sand-coloured ground patch (about 52x14 px) with darker sand speckles, a grey stone block and a small red cross-shaped marker. It is a terrain tile with no standing volume.
top_band: none; this is a flat ground surface, not a standing object, so there is no top band or front face to read in a pixel column
evidence: The candidate is a ground patch seen from above, which is the correct treatment for a terrain kind. It has no standing body, so the 3/4 top-and-front-face contract does not apply. There is no isometric side face and no elevation drawing. The sand fill with tonal speckle reads as a continuous floor surface.

style.evidence: The sand ground has about 3 tones (light sand, mid sand, darker sand) plus a grey pebble and a red-pink accent. Scattered darker clumps and speckle give some texture, with no large 5x5 flat areas. The Beodeul grass and paving references have about 5-6 steps, with clumped tufts and per-stone shading. The candidate is noticeably shallower in ramp depth and tile density: its tiles carry roughly 3-5 colours against about 10 per reference tile. The light-sand speckle is also fairly uniform and noisy, with little structured clumping. A careful artist would see it as thinner than the reference, so it fails on shading depth and density.
